title: A local homomorphism is a colimit of local homomorphisms between essentially finitely generated local rings
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that every local homomorphism of local rings is the colimit of a directed system of local homomorphisms of local rings that are essentially of finite type over Z, respectively over the source (statement lines 32435-32449). The proof does not invoke a presentability theorem for local rings: it indexes the approximations by pairs of finite subsets of the two rings compatible with the homomorphism, builds the subrings they generate, localises at the maximal ideals so that the maps stay local, and then checks that the resulting system is directed with the given map as colimit and with the two finite-type properties (proof lines 32451-32487). Localising at each stage so that locality is preserved is the step that keeps the construction inside the category the statement lives in. H2.
